items.title: Implementing a Humanistic Approach in Akidah Akhlak Learning to Cultivate Students’ Love of Science at MAN 2 Klaten
items.abstract: Objective: This study describes how an Akidah Akhlak teacher applies a humanistic approach at State Islamic Senior High School (Madrasah Aliyah Negeri, MAN) 2 Klaten, Indonesia, and interprets how these practices may support the conditions for students’ love of science. Theoretical framework: The analysis draws on Maslow’s hierarchy of needs, Rogers’ person-centred learning, Freire’s dialogical education and Deci and Ryan’s self-determination theory, and treats hubb al-ʿilm as an Islamic educational orientation that overlaps with, but is not identical to, intrinsic motivation. Literature review: The literature review examines humanistic Islamic education through Maslow, Rogers, Freire, and self-determination theory, highlighting the relationship between student autonomy, emotional needs, moral learning, and hubb al-ʿilm. Research gap: Earlier studies of humanistic Akidah Akhlak learning have mostly examined primary-level madrasahs and moral outcomes such as courtesy and discipline, leaving field evidence on knowledge-oriented outcomes at the Madrasah Aliyah level limited. Methods: A qualitative case study used semi-structured interviews, passive participatory classroom observation and documentation review. Data were analyzed with the interactive model of Miles, Huberman and Saldaña, and credibility was supported by source triangulation and member checking. Results: Three interrelated strategies emerged: differentiating methods according to class conduciveness; negotiating relational agreements that recognize students’ basic needs and autonomy, namely a responsibility-based eating and drinking policy and the absence of homework; and responding to mistakes with mild consequences followed by reflective dialogue on the purpose of seeking knowledge. Together, these practices appear to create a low-threat climate that is conducive to curiosity and to a shift from external towards more internalized motivation. Because the evidence rests mainly on the teacher’s account, supported by classroom observation and documents, the study does not claim that students’ love of science was measured or has increased. Implications: The three-stage model offered here is a contextual interpretation of one case, and may inform teacher reflection and training in comparable madrasahs. Novelty: The study foregrounds hubb al-ʿilm as an affective orientation in humanistic Akidah Akhlak learning at the Madrasah Aliyah level and documents concrete relational agreements that are rarely reported.

items.title: Industrial Emergencies Need a Well Defined “Crisis Communication System” A practitioner-informed exploratory study and framework for high-hazard facilities
items.abstract: Industrial emergencies in refineries, petroleum terminals, chemical plants, and other high-hazard facilities require more than effective firefighting, process isolation, and rescue operations. They also demand timely, accurate, coordinated and stakeholder-specific communication. When information is delayed, inconsistent or inaccessible, operational response may be impeded, families may experience avoidable distress, emergency access may be obstructed, and confidence in the organization may be weakened. This paper examines three practitioner-observed industrial fire emergencies: a refinery fire/explosion in 1988, a fire at Jawahar Dweep in 2017, and a fire emergency encountered during an occupational health, safety, and environment audit. The cases are used as retrospective practitioner illustrations rather than as a statistically representative or conventionally documented qualitative dataset. The paper distinguishes direct observations and recollections from interpretations informed by emergency-communication literature and from the managerial framework proposed by the author. It develops an Industrial Crisis Communication Framework covering preparedness, detection and notification, command and information verification, stakeholder-specific dissemination, monitoring and feedback, and post-emergency learning. Attention is given to family information arrangements, communication redundancy, the separation of operational command channels from public-facing communication, vulnerable stakeholders, misinformation, cyber resilience, and measurable readiness. A preliminary readiness scorecard is proposed for pilot testing in tabletop and full-scale exercises. The framework is intended as a practical, auditable aid for plant-specific emergency preparedness; its effectiveness requires prospective validation.

items.title: Interactive Robots for Accessibility in Diverse Classrooms: A Case of Cantonese Learning for NAS and NCS
items.abstract: Multicultural education in Hong Kong poses learning challenges. For example, non-Chinese-speaking (NCS) students and newly-arrived students (NAS) come from diverse linguistic backgrounds. However, existing interventions emphasise unidirectional instruction. This study addresses the gap by investigating how an interactive robot-assisted scenario (RAS) system can support Cantonese instruction in multicultural classrooms. We employ a mixed-method approach examining quantitative engagement measures and qualitative experiential data. We investigate how RAS intervention can influence the engagement and motivation of NAS and NCS students to learn Cantonese, and the impacts of RAS on the Cantonese proficiency outcomes of NAS and NCS learners. Findings reveal differential engagement patterns: NAS demonstrate improvements in behavioural engagement, while NCS students show a slight decline in cognitive engagement. This research contributes to human-agent interaction (HAI) by examining cross-cultural learning dynamics and providing preliminary insights for the development of multicultural educational technologies.

items.title: Interactive Structured Environment Scaling for Large Language Model Agentic Reasoning
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning via environmental interaction is a cornerstone post-training paradigm for evolving large language models into autonomous agents capable of multi-turn tool use and exploration. Because the environment defines what the policy observes and how actions are verified, its structure directly bounds the capabilities an agent can acquire. Yet existing structured and retrieval environments rely on upstream pre-filtering---extracting a compact subgraph around the gold answer or retrieving fixed passages before the policy acts. We show that such pre-filtering introduces a fundamental measurement confound: because per-question subgraphs enclose ground-truth paths, they compress the candidate space by orders of magnitude and leak answer locations via local topology, allowing a question-blind degree heuristic to surface gold answers far above chance. To restore path selection, candidate pruning, and optimal stopping as genuine policy decisions, we propose RISE (Interactive Structured Environment), which transitions structured reinforcement learning from static subgraphs to full-scale interactive databases along two coupled axes. First, Decision-Space Scaling exposes the unpruned knowledge graph via a five-stage graph-agnostic typed intent adapter under a bounded call budget and a multiplicative grounding reward gate. Second, Learning-Frontier Scaling overcomes within-group variance collapse under group-normalized objectives by uniting model-independent structural tier progression with a self-evolving competence-frontier bandit. Across nineteen benchmarks and three model backbones, RISE substantially advances in-domain and unseen-schema knowledge-graph reasoning, transfers zero-shot to open-domain passage retrieval, and significantly enhances out-of-domain mathematical and logical deduction.

items.title: Interventions Regulating Cognitive Offloading to Generative AI and Subsequent Independent Performance: A Systematic Review Protocol
items.abstract: This systematic review examines interventions designed to regulate cognitive offloading to generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and their effects on subsequent independent performance in educational and employee development contexts. The review aims to identify how interventions structure the distribution of cognitive work between individuals and GenAI, evaluate their effects on learning and task performance after AI assistance has been withdrawn, and examine the conditions under which these effects may differ. Eligible evidence will include comparative experimental and quasi-experimental studies assessing independent knowledge, skills or task performance following GenAI-supported activities. Electronic searches were conducted in six bibliographic databases and preprint repositories, followed by deduplication and pilot screening. Two reviewers will independently screen studies and extract data. The review will use structured descriptive synthesis, supplemented by meta-analysis where the evidence permits. Risk of bias will be assessed using JBI tools, and certainty of evidence for key outcomes will be evaluated using GRADE. The expected contribution is an evidence-based understanding of which approaches to regulating cognitive offloading have been evaluated, what effects they produce on independent performance, and how confidently these effects can be interpreted. Findings may inform the design of GenAI-supported education and employee development activities.

items.title: IsaGraphLib: Formally Verified Efficient Graph Algorithms in Isabelle/HOL
items.abstract: We present a library of formally verified graph algorithms in Isabelle/HOL. The library covers the main problems of combinatorial optimisation on graphs: reachability, shortest paths, minimum spanning trees, matching, maximum flow, and minimum-cost flow. The algorithms in the library use most of the standard algorithm design techniques: graph search, greedy algorithms on matroids, dynamic programming, augmenting paths, blossom contraction, blocking flows, push-relabel, scaling, the primal-dual method, randomisation, and certificate checking. The library has adaptors between different types of graphs (directed, undirected, multigraphs), which allow results to be reused. Each algorithm is verified independently of its data structures, and the main algorithms are refined to efficient imperative implementations, from which we generate code in Standard ML, Scala, and Go. We developed parts of the library with large language models (LLMs), improved the quality of their proofs with a method based on statistics of our own proofs, and labelled which parts were developed by humans, by LLMs, or collaboratively. We perform a detailed experimental analysis of representative algorithms in our library, comparing it with state-of-the-art mainstream libraries, showing that our implementations are practical.

items.title: ISOXIAN Role-Based Implementation Manual: Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100) and Lean Operational Guide for Academic-to-Commercial Medical Device Translation
items.abstract: Overview & Rationale for Structural Redesign The Philippines relies on foreign manufacturers for 99.9% of its medical equipment. While domestic engineering and clinical talent are abundant, academic and local research initiatives frequently stall before reaching clinical deployment due to fragmented workflows, unharmonized regulatory standards, and complex, intimidating Quality Management System (QMS) documentation. Without a clear lifecycle structure, up to 70% of medical equipment in resource-constrained settings fails prematurely due to unaddressed design barriers, missing consumables, or inadequate maintenance pathways. This derivative working manual restructures the comprehensive 21-section ISOXIAN Framework (ISOX-MDR-2026-001) into an actionable, persona-based operational guide designed to shift academic teams from grant-driven prototyping to commercial, regulatory-compliant manufacturing (ISO 13485, ISO 14971, IEC 62366, and PH FDA AO 2020-0010). To maximize comprehension and eliminate cognitive overload for first-time adopters, this edition introduces four structural innovations: Pre-Project Gate 0 (UX Research & Market Validation): Mandates user persona mapping, clinical journey analysis, and target market interviews before engineering resources or procurement are approved, preventing academic teams from building solutions without clinical or commercial viability. Role-Isolated Chapters: Replaces dense cross-functional matrices with dedicated chapters for each project role (Top Management, QMO, PRRC, Product Manager, Project Leader, Hardware/Software Engineers, Clinical/Usability Evaluators, and Asset/IT Administrators). The Toyota Way (Lean Operational Execution): Embeds Genchi Genbutsu (go and see), Jidoka (built-in quality and immediate error stopping), Heijunka (leveled Kanban workflows), and continuous improvement (Kaizen) directly into daily engineering and regulatory tasks. ASD-STE100 (Simplified Technical English): Written using controlled vocabulary, active voice, and strict one-instruction-per-sentence rules to ensure procedures are unambiguous, easily auditable, and executable across multidisciplinary teams without regulatory jargon barriers. items.title: JuryFlow: Disagreement-Guided Human-in-the-Loop Multi-Agent Evaluation
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as automated judges for AI-generated content, yet a single judge is unreliable and even a panel of judges leaves a hard residue: when judges disagree, majority voting simply discards the conflict instead of resolving it. We present JuryFlow, a disagreement-guided, human-in-the-loop multi-agent evaluation framework that treats inter-judge disagreement not as noise to be averaged away, but as a precise, claim-level signal indicating where an evaluation is uncertain. JuryFlow decomposes each candidate response into atomic claims, has a panel of heterogeneous judges assign per-claim verdicts, and builds a disagreement graph whose nodes are scored by verdict entropy and whose edges encode structural similarity between claims. A human acts as a structural guide, i.e., selecting which disagreement to resolve through a single, minimal intervention rather than re-labeling the response, after which the focal claim is re-evaluated, the correction propagates along graph edges and to historically similar cases, and is crystallized into reusable rubric entries that all judges inherit, making the evaluator progressively self-refining. To enable large-scale, reproducible benchmarking without human studies, we evaluate JuryFlow in an automatic configuration in which the focal selection is made by entropy ranking. On MT-Bench and LLMBar, JuryFlow improves agreement with gold labels over single-judge and majority-vote panel baselines, and ablations isolate the contributions of disagreement-targeted re-evaluation, propagation, and rubric induction. We contribute (1) a human-in-the-loop paradigm that recasts the human from labeler to structural guide, (2) the JuryFlow framework operationalizing it through a disagreement graph, focal re-evaluation, and closed-loop rubric induction, and (3) an evaluation protocol with ablations that isolate where the gains originate.

items.title: Kursi Kerja sebagai Komponen Dominan Risiko Ergonomi Berdasarkan Metode ROSA di Universitas Esa Unggul Jakarta
items.abstract: Prolonged computer use may increase ergonomic risk among educational support staff when workplace facilities are not suitable. This study aimed to describe the level of ergonomic risk among 41 educational support staff at Universitas Esa Unggul, Jakarta, using the Rapid Office Strain Assessment (ROSA) method. The study used a cross-sectional design with a descriptive quantitative approach and stratified random sampling. Data were collected through direct observation and ROSA assessment of chair, monitor, telephone, keyboard, and mouse components, then analyzed using frequency distributions and percentages. The results showed that 87.8% of educational support staff were categorized as having high ergonomic risk, while 12.2% were in the moderate-risk category. The highest ROSA score was 7, found in 56.1% of respondents. Problems with the chair component were most frequently found in the armrests and backrests, and all chairs lacked adjustable features for the seat and backrest. These findings indicate the need to improve workplace facilities, particularly chair suitability and adjustability, as part of ergonomic risk control among educational support staff.

items.title: Lao Siji: Adapting openpilot to Closed-Loop End-to-End Driving in Neural Reconstruction
items.abstract: We present Lao Siji, an end-to-end driving policy that ranks third in the 2026 NVIDIA AlpaSim E2E Driving Challenge, ahead of most entries built on foundation models. Instead of training from scratch on a general-purpose vision backbone, we adapt openpilot, an open-source L2 production model. We freeze its vision encoder and fine-tune the policy layers with an ego-state adapter and a route memory. On closed-loop rollouts in neural-reconstructed scenes, we supervise the policy with a privileged map teacher for lateral self-correction and a body-extent loss for road and obstacle clearance, while distilling the base model's remaining outputs to retain car following. Ablations show that self-correction samples carry the gain, while the clearance loss substitutes for them where no teacher exists. Longitudinal safety instead rests on the base model's lead-vehicle estimate behind a rule-based speed layer. Longer training, imitating human logs, and human-log speed targets yield either no measurable gain or adverse effects. Without further training, Lao Siji also places among the leaders on HUGSIM and Odyssey. The final training takes only one GPU-hour and shifts the weights by 3.9% from the shipped model. Code will be released after review.

items.title: Large Language Model-based Optimization for Wireless Communication: A Survey
items.abstract: The growing complexity and dynamism of modern wireless communication frameworks have made real-time optimization essential for efficient resource allocation. Traditional optimization and machine-learning techniques often struggle with generalization, adaptability, stability, and scalability in heterogeneous, time-varying environments. Large language models (LLMs) have recently emerged as powerful tools capable of reasoning over structured prompts and generating context-aware decisions in real time without domain-specific retraining. This survey provides a comprehensive review of LLM-driven optimization techniques applied to wireless communication problems such as power control, bandwidth allocation, task offloading, and intelligent surface configuration. We introduce a functional taxonomy of LLM-enabled wireless resource management strategies and analyze the prompt engineering methodologies employed in recent literature. Furthermore, we develop a generalized analytical framework that categorizes LLM-based optimization architectures, including direct solution generation, closed-loop optimization with external verifiers, and representation encoding within trainable neural pipelines. To demonstrate practical applicability, we present representative case studies on LLM-assisted beam prediction for millimeter-wave systems and adaptive wireless resource allocation. Finally, we discuss emerging hybrid AI approaches for wireless networks.

items.title: LLM-D12: A Dual-Dimensional Scale of Instrumental and Relational Dependencies on Large Language Models
items.abstract: There is growing interest in understanding how people interact with large language models (LLMs) and whether such models elicit dependency or even addictive behaviour. Validated tools to assess the extent to which individuals may become dependent on LLMs are scarce and primarily build on classic behavioural addiction symptoms, adapted to the context of LLM use. We view this as a conceptual limitation, as the LLM-human relationship is more nuanced and warrants a fresh and distinct perspective. To address this gap, we developed and validated a new 12-item questionnaire to measure LLM dependency, referred to as LLM-D12. The scale was based on the authors’ prior theoretical work, with items developed accordingly and responses collected from 526 participants in the UK. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, performed on separate halves of the total sample using a split-sample approach, supported a two-factor structure: Instrumental Dependency (six items) and Relationship Dependency (six items). Instrumental Dependency reflects the extent to which individuals rely on LLMs to support or collaborate in decision-making and cognitive tasks. Relationship Dependency captures the tendency to perceive LLMs as socially meaningful, sentient, or companion-like entities. The two-factor structure demonstrated excellent internal consistency and clear discriminant validity. External validation confirmed both the conceptual foundation and the distinction between the two subscales. The psychometric properties and structure of our LLM-D12 scale were interpreted in light of the emerging view that dependency on LLMs does not necessarily indicate dysfunction but may still reflect reliance levels that could become problematic in certain contexts.

items.title: LLM-Judge Behavioral Coding Scheme for Agent Teammate Quality
items.abstract: Evaluating whether an AI agent behaves like a good teammate is becoming a bottleneck as multi-agent language-model systems proliferate, because human ratings do not scale to the transcripts these systems generate. We ask whether a language model can stand in for a human rater of teammate quality, offering a controlled proof-of-concept validation rather than a large-scale study. Drawing on the autonomous-agent teammate-likeness construct from the human-autonomy-teaming literature, we define a six-dimension behavioral coding scheme covering altruistic, benevolent, interdependent, emotive, communicative, and synchronized conduct, adapted for a language-model judge. We validate it by rewriting the partner’s lines in team-task transcripts as cooperative, neutral, or defective while holding the rest fixed, and having five judges from five model families rate every version. Every judge orders the manipulated behavior as intended and every pair agrees on relative ordering, though absolute calibration differs by up to about a scale point. On registers matched for length and politeness the judges separate cooperative from degraded conduct but resolve subtle defection only weakly; a blinded single-rater human pilot reproduces both the orderings and that limit. The scheme is therefore valid for relative comparisons but not for absolute thresholds applied across judges. We give design implications for LLM-judge teaming evaluation, and release the scheme, stimuli, prompts, and ratings.

items.title: Making Agency Designable: An Engagement Framework for Domestic Digital Twins
items.abstract: Digital Twin (DT) systems are increasingly applied to domestic energy management, distributing decision-making across sensors, algorithms, and users. Designing for shared agency requires making this distribution explicit. This paper characterises engagement in domestic DTs through two lenses: Digital Twin Engagement Style (Visibility × Proactivity) and User Engagement Style (Intentionality × Activeness). These dimensions make system initiative, information visibility, user intentions, and behavioral activity designable. The framework helps designers identify alignments and tensions between user and system engagement, and trace how agency shifts across interaction configurations. Future work will apply the framework to design cases to develop concrete guidelines and assess its practical usefulness.

items.title: MoViC: Real-Time Humanoid Whole-Body Control from Monocular Video Streams
items.abstract: Real-time whole-body imitation from monocular video requires both a robust universal tracker and high-quality real-time reconstruction. We present MoViC, a framework that uses live RGB video as a control signal for humanoid robots without wearable tracking devices. The framework combines monocular human motion reconstruction, robot retargeting, and a transformer-based behavior foundation model. The policy receives proprioceptive history, a single explicit next-step reference, and a compact frequency-domain motion representation that supplies temporal context without explicitly stacking future reference frames, which reduces the input dimension and network size. During deployment, our extrapolation method bridges the 10-Hz visual estimation with 50-Hz controller, enabling asynchronous visual processing and policy execution. Hardware experiments further demonstrate highly dynamic motion tracking and device-free teleoperation of bimanual and single-arm manipulation tasks from live monocular RGB input. items.title: Navigating Dual Responsibilities: Work-Life-Learning Balance Among Master in Business Administration Students in Northeastern College
items.abstract: Balancing employment, graduate education, and personal responsibilities has become a growing challenge for working professionals pursuing advanced degrees in public administration. This phenomenological study explored the lived experiences of Master in Business Administration (MBA) students at Northeastern College, Santiago City, Philippines, in managing work-life-learning balance. Guided by Husserlian phenomenology, the study sought to understand how graduate students navigate competing professional, academic, and personal demands while sustaining academic performance and personal well-being. Purposive sampling was employed to select fifteen MBA students who were simultaneously employed in government agencies, local government units, educational institutions, and private organizations. Data were gathered through semi-structured, in-depth interviews and analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step phenomenological method. Findings revealed five essential themes: (1) navigating competing professional and academic responsibilities; (2) strategic time management and prioritization; (3) institutional and family support as catalysts for persistence; (4) psychological resilience amid multiple role demands; and (5) graduate education as a pathway toward professional advancement and public service excellence. Participants described balancing multiple responsibilities as challenging yet transformative, enabling them to strengthen leadership competencies, decision-making abilities, organizational skills, and public service commitment. Despite experiencing fatigue, stress, and occasional work-life conflicts, students demonstrated resilience through effective planning, support systems, and intrinsic motivation to achieve career advancement. The study underscores the importance of flexible institutional policies, responsive graduate programs, and supportive workplace environments that foster academic persistence among working professionals. The findings contribute to the growing body of literature on adult learning, work-life balance, and graduate education within the context of Philippine public administration.

items.title: NEBench R1: a Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Nuclear Domain Competence in Large Language Models
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being explored for knowledge-intensive and safety-critical applications in nuclear engineering. However, existing nuclear-domain benchmarks provide limited content coverage or focus primarily on answer accuracy without systematically evaluating the quality of the underlying reasoning. This study introduces NEBench R1, a reasoning-oriented benchmark comprising 7,546 unique multiple-choice questions extracted from U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) reactor operator licensing examinations covering 18 nuclear facilities. Each question is classified according to the NRC Knowledge and Abilities catalogs and accompanied by an official explanation serving as a reference for reasoning evaluation. Six LLMs were evaluated, with overall accuracy ranging from 34.0% to 73.9% across three distinct performance tiers. To assess reasoning quality, an LLM-based judge evaluated correctly answered responses using a multidimensional rubric. Although responses generally demonstrated strong problem comprehension, they scored lower in factual and procedural accuracy and distractor analysis, indicating that correct answers were not necessarily supported by technically sound justifications. Response clarity was also weakly indicative of technical quality. Furthermore, longer reasoning traces were associated with lower accuracy in both frontier reasoning models, suggesting that reasoning length may reflect question difficulty rather than improved problem-solving performance. Reasoning-token consumption may therefore provide an additional signal for identifying potentially unreliable responses. NEBench R1 establishes a benchmark for evaluating both answer accuracy and reasoning quality, providing a foundation for assessing the domain competence and reliability of LLMs in nuclear engineering.

items.title: Overhearing AI Deliberation: Reducing Navigation Cost in 2-on-1 AI Interaction
items.abstract: Conversational AI often places navigation cost on users by requiring them to continuously steer conversations, articulate preferences, and monitor AI responses. Reducing this cost may require giving AI systems more conversational initiative, raising questions about how this shift affects users’ agency and responsibility. We explore a 2-on-1 AI deliberation design, where users overhear two agents’ discussion and intervene when needed. Informed by a formative study, our system pairs a Personalized AI representing the user’s preferences with an Expert AI providing alternative perspectives. In a within-subjects mixed-methods study on travel planning, 2-on-1 deliberation reduced navigation cost and perceived agency, while we observed no statistically detectable difference in decision responsibility across conditions. Qualitative findings suggest that users shifted from steering the conversation to overhearing, evaluating, and selectively intervening in agent-to-agent deliberation. We discuss overhearing as an evaluative mode of participation in AI deliberation systems.

items.title: Perceived Authenticity in GenAI‐Mediated Luxury Services: The Role of Delivery Configuration and Need for Uniqueness (NFU)
items.abstract: The growing integration of GenAI into luxury services raises important questions in a domain where exclusivity, authenticity, uniqueness, and human touch are central. Integrating sociotechnical theory with AI‐in‐service and luxury research, this study uses two experiments to examine how human‐only, GenAI‐only, and hybrid luxury service delivery configurations influence customer evaluations. Findings show that hybrid delivery produces the most favorable luxury service outcomes, with perceived authenticity explaining these effects and need for uniqueness (NFU) shaping customer responses across configurations. This research advances understanding of GenAI in luxury services by showing that its value depends on how human and technological capabilities are combined rather than on either mode in isolation. It also contributes to extant knowledge by showing that authenticity is not merely a stable attribute of luxury offerings, but a psychological mechanism affected by how the luxury service is delivered. Finally, it establishes NFU as a motivational boundary condition that explains variation in customer responses to different luxury service delivery configurations and its interplay with perceived authenticity. Practically, this research offers guidance on integrating GenAI in ways that preserve rather than undermine customer evaluations of luxury services.

items.title: Pick Your Poison: Effects of Miscalibrated AI Advice and Silent Updates on Reliance
items.abstract: In AI-assisted decision-making, achieving warranted trust is essential: users should follow accurate advice while rejecting wrong suggestions. But as LLM-based AI agents reshape decision support, such agents often display miscalibrated confidence – ranging from confidently incorrect hallucinations to overly non-committal hedging. To understand how this behavior and unannounced system changes impact user trust, we conducted a two-phase online study (N=90) evaluating advice-seeking and reliance after confidence calibration is silently updated. We found that users’ willingness to seek AI advice is driven overwhelmingly by their pre-existing (positive) attitudes toward AI, not by the system’s prior performance. However, once they actively consult the AI, their reliance is significantly higher if they previously encountered a confidently incorrect or a non-committal system rather than a calibrated baseline. This effect dampens over time, with qualitative insights showing how unannounced background changes can erode perceived quality. These findings demonstrate that safe AI integration requires addressing individual user biases and transparently communicating updates.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

items.title: Production Line Balancing and Cycle Time Optimization in the Motorcycle Manufacturing Industry
items.abstract: The manufacturing industry faces increasing pressure to improve productivity and production efficiency due to growing market demand and competition. Unbalanced workloads among workstations can result in excessive cycle times, bottlenecks, idle time, and line stoppages, which negatively affect production performance. These problems are particularly critical in mass-production systems, where consistent cycle time and balanced workload distribution are essential to maintaining stable production flow. This study focuses on a motorcycle manufacturing line producing automatic motorcycles, where several workstations were identified as having cycle times exceeding the established standard. This study aims to improve production line balance by reducing cycle time deviations, redistributing workloads, and increasing overall line efficiency. The study applies a line balancing approach using the Ranked Positional Weight (RPW) method and a heuristic method. Cycle time data were collected from individual workstations and analyzed to identify overloaded and underutilized stations. The improvement process involved redistributing work elements from overloaded workstations to stations with available capacity, supported by layout adjustments and ergonomic considerations. The target cycle time was set at 22 seconds per workstation. The results show that three workstations initially exceeded the 22 second cycle time standard, with cycle times of 24.77 seconds, 23.28 seconds, and 24.43 seconds. After workload redistribution and process improvements, the cycle times of these workstations were reduced to 21.99 seconds, 21.70 seconds, and 21.87 seconds, respectively. The number of workstations was reduced from 22 to 18. Consequently, line efficiency increased from 81,04 % to 95,06 %, while balance delay decreased from approximately 18.96% to 4,94%. These findings demonstrate that integrating RPW, heuristic workload redistribution, and ergonomic layout improvements can effectively enhance production line balance, reduce bottlenecks, and improve production efficiency. The proposed approach provides a practical framework for continuous line balancing in motorcycle manufacturing and other mass-production environments

items.title: Protecting Safety during Reasoning Training with Low-Rank Fisher Regularisation
items.abstract: Large language models are trained to have safety guardrails, but these can be compromised while fine-tuning for new capabilities, such as reasoning. One way to mitigate this degradation is to modify the fine-tuning objective to preserve safety behaviour, but doing so effectively and efficiently remains challenging. We revisit Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC), which penalises parameter updates based on sensitivity estimates from the diagonal of the Fisher information matrix (FIM). While EWC provides some protection, the diagonal approximation ignores interactions between parameters. We address this limitation by exploiting recent findings that safety-relevant behaviour is located in a low-rank subspace within models. Our method, Subspace-Projected Elastic Weight Consolidation (SP-EWC), projects gradients onto this subspace to capture non-diagonal curvature efficiently. We investigate three different ways of identifying the safety subspace: through safety fine-tuning updates (LoRA), safety-related activations (ActSVD), and contrastive representations of safety and utility data (cPCA). We find that this choice substantially affects performance, with SP-EWC using cPCA comparing favourably against existing methods by better maintaining safety guardrails without introducing excessive over-refusal.

items.title: QGen: Dynamic AI Question Generation During Live Classroom Lectures
items.abstract: University students occasionally struggle to ask questions in class. While AI can support learning, little is known about how it can support in-class question asking. We developed an AI system that generates questions in real time from lecture content and a mobile interface that allows students to view, vote on, and submit their own questions alongside AI-generated ones. We deployed this system in four computer-science lectures, and found that AI-generated questions helped students consider lecture content from different perspectives. For some, this prompted deeper reflection on what to ask. However, others reported reduced motivation to form their own questions, suggesting risks of overreliance. Although students found the AI helpful, they more frequently voted for questions asked by their peers, revealing a gap between AI-generated questions and students’ in-the-moment learning needs. We provide design recommendations for systems that promote interactive collaboration with AI and scaffold question asking without undermining student agency.

items.title: Reflection Is Not Always Worth It: Budgeted Reflection Allocation for Recommendation Agents
items.abstract: This work aims to make recommendation agents more efficient by reducing unnecessary LLM reflection while preserving full-catalog ranking and inference reranking. Since BRAVE changes only how training-time reflection is allocated, it does not introduce new user data requirements or additional LLM exposure beyond the base agent protocol. The main potential risk is that a poorly calibrated allocator may assign less reflection to users whose preferences are sparse, niche, or under-represented, which could weaken personalization for those users or indirectly affect item exposure. This risk can be mitigated through deployment-time auditing and conservative allocation design. In practice, reflection budgets should be evaluated not only by aggregate Recall or NDCG, but also across user-history lengths, item popularity groups, and application-relevant cohorts when such analysis is permitted. The allocator should rely on task-side ranking evidence rather than sensitive attributes, and fallback policies can reserve a small portion of the budget for random or fairness-aware coverage when subgroup robustness is important. Privacy risks can be controlled with the same protections required by the base recommendation agent: minimizing user text sent to the LLM controller, anonymizing user identifiers, retaining only necessary interaction evidence, and applying standard access-control and logging policies. Overall, BRAVE is designed as a cost-aware allocation layer, and its ethical deployment depends on validating that the saved computation does not come at the expense of vulnerable users or responsible exposure.

items.title: Relación entre el marketing de contenidos de formato corto en TikTok/Instagram Reels y el engagement cognitivo-afectivo en usuarios universitarios de Quito, Ecuador
items.abstract: Short-form video content marketing, driven by recommendation algorithms on platforms such as TikTok and Instagram Reels, has drastically transformed digital interaction patterns among young populations. The objective of this research was to analyze the relationship between short-form content marketing on TikTok and Instagram Reels and cognitive-affective engagement among university users in the Metropolitan Area of Quito, Ecuador. A quantitative, cross-sectional, and correlational-explanatory study was carried out on a stratified probabilistic sample of N = 480 university students (52.1% female, 47.9% male) aged between 18 and 28 years (M = 21.45, SD = 2.18). Data collection was performed using a structured questionnaire comprising 24 validated items on a 5-point Likert scale, which registered optimal reliability indices (Cronbach's Alpha α = .912 and McDonald's Omega ω = .925). The inferential procedure included Pearson and Spearman correlation coefficients, analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), adjusted multivariable logistic regression, and structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) processed in Python and SPSS v28. The results demonstrated a strong positive correlation between algorithmic content relevance and cognitive engagement (r = .642, p < .001) and affective engagement (r = .685, p < .001). The logistic modeling confirmed that high exposure to short-form educational and user-generated content substantially increases the probability of high purchase intention (OR = 4.28, 95% CI: 2.45-7.48).

items.title: Research on the Transformation of College English Translation Teaching Driven by Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: In response to the current predicaments faced by university English translation teaching in the era of artificial intelligence, such as narrowed goals, fixed content, monotonous models, lagging evaluation, and the absence of AI literacy among teachers and students, this study has constructed a transformation analysis framework covering five dimensions: goal positioning, content organization, teaching model, evaluation method, and teacher-student roles. Based on this framework, a four-stage process-oriented teaching model of "AI pre-translation - comparative diagnosis - post-translation editing - reflection and summary" for human-machine collaboration has been proposed. The study adopts a quasi-experimental design and implements a 12-week teaching intervention for 82 non-English major undergraduate students at a certain university. The experimental results show that the post-test translation scores and post-translation editing abilities of the experimental class are significantly better than those of the control class; at the same time, the experimental class also shows significant improvements in various dimensions of AI usage strategies, the accuracy of critical judgment, the level of intrinsic motivation, and the perception of task value. The analysis based on qualitative data further confirms the positive changes in students' awareness of strategies, repositioning of human-machine roles, and enhanced metacognitive monitoring. In summary, these findings indicate that structured human-machine collaborative training can simultaneously enhance translation quality, process strategy level, and learning motivation quality, providing an evidence-based basis and operational practical paths for the digital transformation of university English translation teaching.

items.title: Research progress on spray dust suppression mechanisms and synergistic enhancement technologies in mines
items.abstract: Mine dust poses serious occupational health and safety risks in mining operations. Traditional water-spraying dust suppression methods have limitations: within the “Greenfield gap,” the effects of inertial collision, interception, and Brownian motion diffusion are significantly reduced; furthermore, the hydrophobic nature of mine dust further diminish dust suppression effectiveness. This bottleneck stems from inherent water-dust interface properties, and adjusting pressure or nozzle settings alone has limited effectiveness. This paper systematically analyzes the basic mechanisms of traditional spray dust suppression, including atomization, collision, wetting, and sedimentation, to identify core efficiency bottlenecks. It reviews two dimensions of synergistic enhancement: chemical modifications (surfactants, polymers, foam dust suppressants, nanomaterials, microorganisms, and functional dust suppressants) and physical external field coupling (acoustic fields, magnetized water, micro-nano bubbles, and electrostatic charges), detailing their mechanisms, advantages, and limitations. These technologies successfully overcome traditional constraints. Specifically, an integrated “physical external field + chemical medium” approach generates a multi-level synergistic mechanism, substantially improving dust capture efficiency under complex working conditions. It further maps applicability onto four mine types, assessing energy demand, cost, environmental and safety burden and implementation maturity. However, shortcomings remain: insufficient quantitative analysis of process coupling mechanisms, high energy consumption associated with synergistic enhancement, and engineering constraints, as well as poor adaptability to complex mining environments. Therefore, future work should focus on developing cross-scale, multi-physics models to quantitatively analyze liquid-phase coupling and the permeation threshold of the gas film; developing green functional materials that have undergone life cycle assessment; and achieving intelligent, adaptive spray control.

items.title: Risk-certified prompt optimization for LLM-as-a-judge guardrails
items.abstract: LLM-as-a-judge guardrails are often controlled primarily through system prompts, yet standard prompt optimization methods target average performance rather than explicit safety constraints. This paper studies system-prompt selection as a constrained optimization problem: maximize benign pass rate while keeping the missed-attack rate below a user-specified level α with finite-sample statistical control. The framework combines LLM-based judging, automatic prompt generation, and distribution-free risk certification. This work instantiates it in two procedures: CPS and CRISP. CPS generates a fixed pool of prompts from training data, then certifies candidates on a held-out evaluation set using simultaneous upper confidence bounds and selects the certified prompt with the highest benign utility. CRISP instead integrates risk feedback into an adaptive search, using hard example-guided rewriting and a reusable-holdout interface to steer generation toward the feasible utility frontier. Experiments on four datasets covering prompt injection, system-prompt leakage, and sensitive-information disclosure show that risk-certified selection consistently respects the target missed-attack level on heldout tests, while utility improves as the permitted risk is relaxed. CRISP is especially useful when fixed-pool search fails to produce certifiable high-utility candidates.

items.title: Sangyadhi: An Analytical Framework for Diagnosing and Investigating Collective Care
items.abstract: While HCI has expanded from Personal to Family Informatics, researchers still lack a critical analytical vocabulary to diagnose what truly constitutes a collective care context. We introduce Sangyadhi, an analytical sociotechnical framework that synthesizes Situated Action, Distributed Cognition, the Capabilities Approach, and Actor-Network Theory to investigate multi-actor care ecologies. The framework articulates four interdependent analytical lenses: contextual grounding, distributed responsibility, trust-mediated sharing, and collaborative actionability. To demonstrate its diagnostic utility, we apply Sangyadhi to critically audit a decade of HCI digital health literature across self-tracking, family informatics, and clinical AI---surfacing structural omissions in how shifting authority, dynamic trust, and AI escalation are conceptualized. Ultimately, the goal of Sangyadhi is to equip researchers with an analytical blueprint for diagnosing observed care contexts, structuring field inquiries, and evaluating future technologies.

items.title: Saúde mental dos profissionais portuários: riscos psicossociais, prevenção e qualidade de vida no trabalho
items.abstract: Port work involves complex operations, productivity demands, exposure to occupational hazards and, in some roles, shifts and working hours that may contribute to physical and emotional strain. This article aims to analyze occupational and psychosocial factors related to the mental health of port workers and discuss prevention measures and the promotion of quality of working life. A qualitative, exploratory and descriptive bibliographic study was conducted, drawing on scientific articles, literature reviews, institutional documents and occupational health and safety regulations. The analysis identified relevant factors such as work overload, intense pace, noise, accident risks, irregular shifts, limited autonomy and insufficient social support. The literature indicates that prevention should integrate physical, ergonomic and psychosocial risks, with workers’ participation and organizational commitment. As an educational dissemination activity, the topic was also presented at EXPOTEC 2026 through an exhibition and interactive activities. This experience encouraged dialogue and the sharing of perceptions, but did not constitute field research or a systematic assessment of companies. The article concludes that protecting mental health in the port sector requires continuous risk management, communication, support and improvements in working conditions and work organization.

items.title: Scaling large language model-assisted line-of-therapy adjudication with human-in-the-loop evidence-calibrated selection
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have enabled the ability to scale clinical adjudication tasks traditionally dependent on exhaustive manual review. Line-of-therapy (LoT) adjudication, a major bottleneck in oncology cohort construction, is a prime example. Line boundaries must be inferred from longitudinal treatment histories according to nuanced, study-specific definitions, at every regimen transition for every patient. LLMs can apply this adjudication at scale, but their reliability varies across patients. Treatment histories differ in complexity, and ambiguous or atypical patterns depend on expert clinical judgment. Reliable automation thus requires verified support for model assignments and the ability to identify cases that warrant manual review. Here, we present evidence-calibrated selection (ECS), a human-in-the-loop framework for scaling LLM-assisted LoT adjudication. ECS derives confidence from observed clinician adjudications, prioritizes patients with the least-supported assignments for follow-up review, and returns completed adjudications to the model as precedent. As the evidence base grows, ECS continuously calibrates confidence to estimate residual error, thus enabling more efficient use of clinician time. In simulations on 136 clinician adjudicated patients with multiple myeloma, ECS achieved a residual error of 5% after review of 44.6% of patients, compared to 62.2% when review was directed by LLM self-reported confidence and 81.9% under random sampling. These results support a scalable approach to study-specific LoT adjudication, using clinician evidence to inform automated predictions, minimize error, and reduce review burden.

items.title: Score-Based Stochastic Closure Modeling via Offline Indirect Learning and Online Data Assimilation
items.abstract: Stochastic closure modeling is an emerging area in reduced-order modeling of large and complex (e.g., multiscale, multi-physics) systems, for which the computationally affordable reduced-order physical descriptions (e.g., digital twins for additive manufacturing, world models for AI agents) in numerical simulations inevitably lead to information losses that cannot be well addressed by classical deterministic closures. However, learning stochastic closures typically requires closure data that are difficult to obtain from measurements or often prohibitively expensive to compute using first-principles simulations. In this work, we develop a stochastic closure modeling framework that builds on score-based diffusion models, leveraging indirect offline training and online data assimilation without requiring the direct data of closures. Numerical experiments on two-dimensional turbulent flows demonstrate that indirect offline learning captures key closure statistics and improves predictions of system state. In addition, combining the learned closure with known physical dynamics leads to better generalization capability across different regimes than purely data-driven models that directly predict system state. Compared to standard data assimilation methods with a Gaussian assumption, the posterior-score assimilation better represents non-Gaussian features of the learned closure, and its combination with state-level data assimilation further improves prediction of the system state. The proposed framework enables stochastic closure modeling in realistic and challenging scenarios of complex dynamical systems in mechanics and engineering problems, where non-Gaussian statistics of model-form uncertainties are non-negligible (e.g., due to the nonlinearities of the system dynamics and/or the observations) and true closure data are not available, for both offline learning and online assimilation.

items.title: Self-perceived happiness and integrative community therapy among slaughterhouse workers in a Brazilian municipality on an international border
items.abstract: Objective: To analyze the effects of Integrative Community Therapy (ICT) on self-perceived happiness and emotional well-being among slaughterhouse workers in a Brazilian municipality located on an international border. Methods: This exploratory quasi-experimental study was grounded in the ICT framework and conducted in Itaipulândia, Paraná, from April to December 2019. The McDowell and Newell Faces Scale was used to assess self-perceived happiness before and after ICT circles, alongside a sociodemographic questionnaire and an analysis of universal themes and coping strategies that emerged during the circles. Results: Twelve circles were held with 151 workers. Self-perceived happiness and emotional state improved significantly after the circles. The main universal themes were physical health problems, bereavement, family conflict, and stress, revealing the connection between emotional suffering and the work context. The most common coping strategies were seeking spiritual or religious support, strengthening family relationships, and personal empowerment. Workers aged 18–24 years had 4.28 times greater odds of emotional improvement after participating in the circles than workers older than 24 years. Conclusion: ICT showed promise as a relationship-centered care strategy in occupational health, supporting improved self-perceived happiness and emotional well-being and strengthening support networks among slaughterhouse workers. Collective and integrative care strategies may be particularly valuable in work settings marked by physical and psychosocial vulnerability.

items.title: SGIP: Learning Scene-Grounded Interaction Priors for Scene-Aware Human Motion Prediction
items.abstract: Human motion prediction (HMP) aims to forecast future movement from an observed motion sequence, and recent methods have incorporated 3D scene geometry and object semantics to improve long-term plausibility. However, the destination of future motion remains ambiguous in cluttered scenes: the same observed motion can lead to different interaction targets or navigation modes. Existing methods either handle this ambiguity implicitly or rely on auxiliary signals like gaze that are hard to obtain in practice. To address this, we propose SGIP, which explicitly predicts where in the scene future motion will be grounded across both objects and open navigation regions, and uses it to condition future trajectory and full-body pose prediction. This scene-grounded interaction prior is learned via intent distillation: at training time only, a teacher model scores candidate scene regions by combining an LLM prompted with a textual description of the person's intent with geometric motion-scene features. A student model learns to reproduce these scores from only the observed motion and 3D scene, making intent and LLM unnecessary at test time. Across multiple benchmark datasets, SGIP outperforms prior scene-aware baselines on both trajectory and pose accuracy in a realistic deployment setting where neither gaze nor intent is available at inference, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The project page is available at https://sgip2026.github.io.

items.title: Socrates went nuclear: Comparing Interaction Strategies for AI systems in a Learning Context using Brain Sensing
items.abstract: Students are adopting LLMs at scale. This poses a question: does unrestricted AI access bypass the cognitive effort required for learning, or does it streamline knowledge acquisition? This paper reports on a study where we compare three designs for user-AI interaction in a learning context: (1) an unrestricted conversational bot like ChatGPT, (2) a pedagogically constrained bot that guides through hints without giving final answers, which we refer to as the Socratic mode; and (3) a non-conversational adaptive tutoring system that adjusts difficulty in real-time based on the user’s cognitive engagement derived from the brain signals. Fifty study participants were tasked with learning about nuclear safety protocols, a domain chosen for its zero-prior knowledge baseline. The participants progressed through an instructional video, a pre-test, an AI-driven assessment phase, which varied in the three conditions, and an immediate post-test. The nature of the questions centered primarily on factual knowledge acquisition, but it still required participants to have a global understanding of the concepts in order to answer the questions correctly. A Muse headband was used to derive the cognitive engagement of all users in all conditions. The unrestricted chatbot produced higher learning gains (delta) than both constrained modes ( p <.03, d > 0.80), while the adaptive condition generated significantly higher EEG engagement ( p =.018). The cluster analysis of chatbot usage and discussion patterns by users showed that most participants in the unrestricted-mode adopted a direct answer-retrieval strategy, while participants in the Socratic-mode initially attempted to reason through the hints before progressively disengaging. Consequently, this also suggests that the success of the unrestricted AI is not an evidence of deeper learning, but rather a result of the immediate post-test evaluation after the training phase.

items.title: Take a Step Back: A Dual-Granularity Raw Feature Empowered Intermediate Fusion Graph Convolutional Network for Multimodal Recommendation
items.abstract: Although multimodal recommendations have shown the ability to learn user preferences and item properties by leveraging explicit multimodal information, they remain constrained by two critical limitations: low-quality representation learning and modality fusion. For the former, existing solutions primarily focus on multi-granularity representation learning; however, we argue that training such representations is difficult due to the inherent data sparsity problem in recommendation scenarios. For the latter, existing solutions often rely on contrastive learning to align representations of different modalities to facilitate modality fusion, yet alignment-only objectives may over-compress valuable modality-specific information. To this end, we suggest \underline{``Take a Step Back"} and propose a \textbf{D}ual-granularity raw feature empowered \textbf{I}ntermediate fusion \textbf{G}raph \textbf{C}onvolutional \textbf{N}etwork (\textbf{DIGCN}) for multimodal recommendation. DIGCN leverages the multimodal understanding capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) to construct dual-granularity raw features directly. Furthermore, DIGCN introduces an intermediate fusion graph convolutional network equipped with dynamic cross-modality weight correction, designed to capture cross-modality signals and achieve effective modality fusion. Comprehensive experiments on four real-world datasets validate that DIGCN consistently outperforms a variety of strong baselines. Additional analyses confirm its superiority under varying levels of data sparsity and cold-start scenarios. Notably, DIGCN demonstrates high extensibility, capable of further benefiting from additional contrastive learning-based alignment tasks.

items.title: Technical competence, occupational health and safety, and environment predict contractor employee performance
items.abstract: Applied studies of employee performance in Indonesian technical firms usually ask which factor dominates. This study asks instead whether technical competence, occupational health and safety (OHS), and the work environment behave as rival levers or as a bundle of resources. A census survey of all 41 employees of PT Multi Jaya Teknik, an electrical and mechanical contractor in Batu Bara Regency, North Sumatra, measured each construct with a five-item Likert scale (α = .807-.903), and performance was regressed on the three predictors by ordinary least squares. The predictors jointly explained a large share of variance, R² = .602 (adjusted R² = .570), F(3, 37) = 18.65, p < .001. Technical competence (B = 0.372, 95% CI [0.035, 0.709], f² = 0.135), OHS (B = 0.290, 95% CI [0.048, 0.532], f² = 0.159), and work environment (B = 0.261, 95% CI [0.018, 0.504], f² = 0.127) each retained a unique positive association, with closely matched standardized weights (β = .267-.335) and overlapping intervals. Because the smallest individual effect the design could detect was f² = 0.202, each estimate is individually fragile, whereas the joint effect is clear. The pattern is interpreted as safe competence: in hazardous field work, capability, safety provision, and workable conditions act as non-redundant resources, so no single lever should be expected to dominate. The study also shows that perceived OHS provision predicts self-rated performance, not accident prevention, and it offers a complete reporting template for small single-firm samples.

items.title: The Delegation Boundary: Willingness to Delegate to AI Agents Depends on Retained Override More Than on Domain
items.abstract: What people hand over to an AI agent has a boundary: a point at which advice becomes action taken on their behalf. We examine that distinction across six agent scenarios rated by 296 U.S. adults, analyzed as 3 (domain) × 2 (advisory versus substitutive). Advisory scenarios received higher ratings in each domain, with a larger partial η2 for scenario category than for domain (.465 versus.053). The contrast was positive in every subgroup examined, but domain-specific differences showed low internal consistency (α =.08), giving limited support for a single cross-domain tendency. Objective AI knowledge and awareness of model limitations were associated with overall willingness in opposite directions. These vignette contrasts do not isolate a causal effect of retained override.

items.abstract: Hospitals and health systems are complex adaptive systems. Safe care, continuity of services and the ability to adapt under pressure all depend on people noticing what is happening, making sense of it and anticipating what comes next. Situational awareness (SA), a concept that grew out of military aviation and human factors engineering, is now built into clinical non-technical skills frameworks, organisational resilience models and crisis management practice.

items.title: THE ROLE OF HEALTH LITERACY IN PREVENTING OCCUPATIONAL DISEASES AMONG MINERS
items.abstract: This article examines the role of health literacy in preventing occupational diseases among miners in Uzbekistan. It focuses on miners’ ability to understand workplace health information, apply it during routine tasks, and communicate concerns to supervisors and occupational health professionals. Using exposure to respirable dust and excessive noise as examples, the article considers how miners can interpret the purpose of exposure controls, report problems with protective measures, and understand the role of periodic health examinations. It also examines how plain-language instructions, practical demonstrations, and asking workers to explain procedures in their own words can help occupational health teams identify misunderstandings during training. Health literacy is considered alongside engineering controls, exposure monitoring, and health surveillance within a workplace prevention programme. For medical students, the article illustrates how occupational health consultations can connect a miner’s work history with the hazards encountered on the job and communicate preventive measures in terms relevant to the worker’s daily tasks.

items.title: The Scientific Approach as an Accelerator of Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Healthcare: The LifeLink Monitoring Mode
items.abstract: This article asks how a scientific, evidence-generating approach can speed up the adoption of artificial intelligence in healthcare. We use LifeLink Monitoring as an applied case and combine a structured literature review, market and regulatory analysis, competitive benchmarking, stakeholder surveys and expert interviews, scenario modelling, and pilot design. The analysis reveals a persistent shortage of context-specific evidence on clinical utility, workflow integration, human factors, economics, and governance. To address it, we propose an Evidence-to-Adoption Framework in which staged pilots turn technological hypotheses into evidence that clinicians, managers, regulators, payers, and investors can act on. We treat acceleration as a proposed mechanism that requires prospective testing, not as a demonstrated outcome, and we specify how it can be measured.

items.title: Towards a foundation model for Type IIB flux vacua
items.abstract: Progress in characterising the Type IIB flux landscape requires scalable methods for constructing flux vacua. In this work, we investigate generative models as a framework for sampling vacua across multiple Calabi-Yau geometries and for directing searches towards specified physical properties. We compare transformers and diffusion models trained to generate quantised fluxes together with approximate values of the complex structure moduli and axio-dilaton. We exploit a staged training procedure comprising pre-training, and post-training via reinforcement learning, and assess how each stage improves the generated distributions and enables targeted sampling. We further examine whether structures learned from geometries with smaller $h^{1,2}$ can be transferred to geometries with larger $h^{1,2}$ through fine-tuning on specialised datasets. Our results provide evidence that generative models can learn distributions of flux vacua across distinct compactifications, improve searches for vacua with selected properties and transfer information between geometries. This establishes a concrete basis for developing a foundation model of the Type IIB flux landscape.

items.title: Towards Agentic Scientific Discovery in Distributed Systems
items.abstract: We investigate when adaptive tool selection helps identify a shared equation across clients with different input coverage. Query-ATLAS (query-conditioned Agentic Tool-based Learning for Aggregating Symbolic Equations) uses an LLM to guide symbolic search from client errors and previous proposals in a simulated distributed system. A four-architecture comparison reveals task-dependent opportunities: relative to fixed PySR-LLM, validation acceptances rise from 3/12 to 7/12 on CRK3 and from 11/12 to 12/12 on oscillator2, while MatSci3 favors the fixed workflow. Across 72 settings in a post-hoc six-task subset of eight development tasks, Query-ATLAS achieves 64 validation and 64 in-distribution passes, versus 62 and 59 for the fixed workflow; both pass 47/60 eligible out-of-distribution tests. The fixed workflow retains lower median errors and cost. Broader query coverage emerges as a promising benefit, motivating task-aware tool selection and client-aware fitting for scientific agents.

items.title: Translating Multi-Agent Traffic Logic into On-Demand Human-Vehicle Dialogue
items.abstract: Unsignalized roundabouts remain challenging for connected and autonomous vehicles because of dynamic merges, spatial conflicts, and communication constraints. We present a decentralized coordination architecture based on Group Mutual Exclusion (GME), in which each conflict point is treated as a local critical section and compatible virtual platoons may be admitted concurrently. A lead vehicle aggregates requests from its physical queue and relays admission decisions to following vehicles. To make this safety-critical process intelligible to occupants, we introduce a query-driven small language model (SLM) interface that reads structured controller traces and produces explanations only when requested. The SLM is strictly read-only and cannot alter GME decisions. We illustrate how traces containing conflict, priority, and waiting-time information can support contextual explanations of yielding, deceleration, and merging. The work provides an architecture and feasibility demonstration. Quantitative traffic, language-model, and human-factors evaluations are left to future work.

items.title: TRANSLATING POWER: AI, MEDIATION AND THE IMAGINARY OF MANIPULATION IN ACADEMIC CONTEXTS
items.abstract: The growing use of generative artificial intelligence in academic writing and translation is changing not only the speed of textual production but also the ways in which linguistic authority is constructed and perceived. In multilingual academic contexts, AI systems translate, reformulate, and refine texts according to dominant conventions of academic English. Such assistance may widen access to international communication, yet its fluency can also make the interpretative choices embedded in the resulting text less visible. This article examines AI-mediated Romanian-English academic translation as a site where linguistic assistance, symbolic power, and the imaginary of manipulation intersect. The study approaches translation as mediation rather than neutral transfer. It asks how AI may reshape lexical authority, epistemic stance, and stylistic identity, how these changes influence the perceived legitimacy of academic discourse, and when unobtrusive mediation may acquire a potentially manipulative effect. The theoretical discussion connects translation studies with scholarship on symbolic power, academic stance, and sociotechnical imaginaries. Methodologically, the article adopts a conceptual qualitative approach supported by three illustrative Romanian-English micro-analyses. These examples are not treated as a representative corpus and do not support statistical generalisation. Instead, they reveal how apparently minor lexical, epistemic, and stylistic reformulations can influence authority, certainty, and authorial visibility. The article argues that manipulation should not be equated automatically with factual distortion or deliberate ideological intent. It may also arise through naturalisation, when a fluent and plausible formulation is accepted as transparent or inevitable. The article concludes that responsible AI-assisted academic translation requires comparison with the source, attention to shifts in certainty, agency and rhetorical positioning, and clear human responsibility for the final text. For translators, writers and educators, critical AI literacy entails treating generated language as a proposal to be evaluated rather than as an impersonal solution.

items.title: Trust and Fatigue Diverge in Predicting Verification Behavior and Use Frequency in AI-Mediated Information Environments
items.abstract: Reliance on artificial agents involves at least two decisions: whether to use the system and whether to verify its output. We examined how trust and self-reported verification fatigue were associated with these dimensions in survey responses from 390 adults across six English-speaking countries. Trust was strongly associated with AI use frequency (β =.50), whereas verification fatigue was not (β =.05). Fatigue was instead associated with verification skipping (β =.36) and selective verification (β =.31) but not reliably with active verification, and these two coefficients did not differ (Δβ =.05, p =.382). Trust was associated only with skipping among the three effort-graded verification behaviors, and its coefficient was larger for skipping than for selective verification (Δβ =.12, p =.040). No interaction survived correction. This pattern is consistent with trust relating to perceived verification necessity and self-reported verification fatigue to perceived verification burden, two routes converging on verification skipping; however, the cross-sectional self-report design cannot establish these mechanisms.

items.title: Turning Errors into Successes: Designing LLM Tutoring Around Scaffolded Error Correction
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) could make personalized tutoring available at scale, but it remains unclear how they can best support the instructional processes that make one-on-one instruction effective. We compared two ways of using LLMs after students make errors: providing personalized explanations of those errors, or engaging students in additional cycles of scaffolded practice and feedback, with a Socratic tutor guiding students toward the correct answer. In a preregistered online experiment, 400 adults practiced setting up constraint equations and, after each attempt, received the correct answer, a generic explanation, a personalized LLM explanation of their error, or Socratic tutoring. Socratic tutoring helped: participants resolved 64% of their errors through the dialogue and scored 0.24 SD higher on practice-aligned posttest questions than those who received generic or personalized explanations. Socratic participants also found the session more interesting, less frustrating, and less costly, even though it took nearly twice as long. In contrast, we found no evidence of a benefit of personalized explanations over generic ones, and neither type of explanation reliably outperformed simply seeing the correct answer. These findings suggest that LLM tutors may add the most value not by explaining errors more precisely but by helping students correct those errors themselves through scaffolded practice. This pattern fits a mastery-experience account of tutoring, in which an effective tutor notices when a student is struggling, steps in with guidance, and works with the student until the struggle resolves into success. AI tutors may be most effective when designed around this principle.
topics: Intelligent Tutoring Systems and Adaptive Learning

items.title: Understanding Users' Security, Privacy, and Trust Concerns in Healthcare AI Systems
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated into healthcare systems, from clinical information retrieval to workflow automation and decision support, which introduces new security, privacy, and trust risks with direct implications for patient care. While prior work has examined these risks from technical and regulatory perspectives, less is known about how these risks are naturally discussed in online communities. To address this gap, we conduct a large-scale analysis of 14 medical communities on Reddit and extract 6,514 relevant posts. Through systematic qualitative coding and LLM-assisted classification, we investigate concerns expressed in healthcare AI discussions, their prevalence, and how they evolve over time. Our analysis reveals that users perceive healthcare AI as expanding traditional healthcare trust boundaries and attack surfaces through integrations with electronic health records, third-party services, cloud platforms, and automated clinical workflows. Posts express concerns about over-privileged access to sensitive records, opaque data flows, unauthorized secondary use, and unsafe automation can amplify the consequences of errors and misuse. We identify four attitudes toward these risks: exploring questions of accountability and harm, cautiously accepting AI with stronger safeguards, skepticism about system trustworthiness, and resignation to growing data exposure and automation. Longitudinal analysis shows that SP&T discussions have increased significantly, with shifts coinciding with major healthcare AI deployments, privacy incidents, and regulatory developments. These findings illuminate changing trust relationships and data-governance challenges, informing the design and governance of safer, more transparent, and accountable healthcare AI systems.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

items.title: Vibe Interventions: Can Users Personalize and Iterate Their Way to Behavior Change?
items.abstract: Recent advances in large language models allow a working application to be generated from natural-language description, and is referred to as generative user interfaces. Their application to behavior change is unexplored, and we provide one of the first controlled investigations of it. We distinguish two components of authorship: iteration, the revision of a generated artifact in natural language, and personalization, the conditioning of generation on stated context. In a pre-registered between-subjects experiment (N = 300, 60 per condition), we crossed these two factors and added a static intervention as a control, yielding five conditions; participants stated a goal and received a generated intervention. The personalized generative condition ranked highest on every self-report outcome, including ownership, satisfaction, and intended adoption. Randomized iteration had no detectable effect, and higher revision counts were negatively associated with evaluative ratings. This work establishes which component of authorship carries motivational value in generative behavior change tools.
